summary: Full backend + frontend testing of Getaride Orlando (fresh MVP). Backend: 22/22 pytest tests passing across auth (register/login/me), customer ride flow (create ride, progressive 5-offer reveal sorted by fare ascending, select offer -> driver_enroute, live tracking with simulated location), driver flow (online toggle, simulated requests, bid range validation, ~5s auto-accept, status progression arrived->in_progress->completed), chat with auto-reply, history endpoints (/me/rides, /driver/trips), and /places search. Frontend: end-to-end mobile UI flows verified at 390x844 mobile viewport via Playwright. Customer signup -> place picker (Walt Disney World) -> Find Rides -> 5 driver offer cards visible (fare/eta/rating) -> Accept -> live tracking screen with chat. Chat send + auto-reply ('I'm pulling up now.') works. Driver signup -> Go Online -> 5 nearby requests appear -> Set Fare opens bid sheet with $ stepper showing allowed range -> Submit Bid -> after ~5s auto-accept routed to driver-trip screen 'Head to pickup' -> I've Arrived advances arrived -> Start Trip -> Complete. Purple branding consistent. No red-screen errors. Minor non-blocking React-Native-Web warnings observed: deprecated 'shadow*' style props and deprecated props.pointerEvents.

issues: RN-Web console warning: shadow* style props deprecated (theme.ts L54-65). Consider switching to boxShadow for web parity. Cosmetic only.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Likely from a third-party RN-Web layer or one of the screens. Non-blocking but should be silenced to keep logs clean.

action_items: Optional polish: replace shadowColor/shadowOffset/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius in /app/frontend/src/theme.ts with cross-platform boxShadow (or guard with Platform.OS !== 'web') to clear RN-Web deprecation warnings.
Optional polish: track down the 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' warning and migrate to style.pointerEvents.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single ~590-line file. Still acceptable for MVP, but consider splitting into routers (auth, customer, driver, chat) as features grow.

compute_track auto-completes a ride 85s after acceptance regardless of driver-driven status updates; manual driver status updates can be overwritten by /track polling. Acceptable for simulated MVP but worth a guard if drivers shouldn't be auto-completed.

select_offer does not check that the requesting customer owns the ride (any authenticated user can select an offer on any ride). Same for cancel_ride and track. Low-risk for MVP but should be tightened before production.
register stores email lowercased server-side; FE should mirror lowercase for any client-side comparisons (no current bug observed).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of critical flows (customer signup->offers->accept->track->chat; driver online->bid->auto-accept->advance to completed)

seed_data_creation: Tests register fresh TEST_-prefixed users each run; relies on simulated driver offers and simulated open requests seeded server-side on driver/online and /driver/requests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend base URL is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env (https://nextjs-rebuild-8.preview.emergentagent.com). All endpoints under /api. Bearer-JWT auth via /api/auth/register or /api/auth/login. Driver bid auto-accepts ~5s after submission; full ride completes ~85s after accept via /api/rides/{id}/track polling. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_getaride_backend.py for regression. For UI, all critical testIDs are present (auth-submit, role-customer/driver, find-rides, destination-row, place-option-<label>, offer-<id>, accept-<id>, open-chat, chat-input, chat-send, go-online/online-toggle, bid-<rideId>, fare-plus/minus, submit-bid, advance-status).
rca_of_issue: N/A - no blocking bugs found in this iteration.
